shortName: Sidney Kimmel Medical College at Thomas Jefferson University
additionalCoursework: Exposure to the Humanities, English, and the Behavioral Sciences is also encouraged. Applicants can select various courses in these areas of study to broaden their overall educational experience.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: SKMC defines diversity as the richness in human differences. Applications from qualified students with diverse experiences and backgrounds are encouraged.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Under certain circumstances, leaves of absence may be granted to students who are in good academic standings.  These leaves may be for medical problems, for academic enrichment or for personal non-medical reasons.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Students have many opportunities to participate in various medical societies and service organizations.  The University Activities Office coordinates social, cultural and recreational programs for the Jefferson Community.  The Student Organization Directory includes descriptions of more than 100 campus organizations and groups.  
https://www.jefferson.edu/life-at-jefferson/activities-and-organizations/student-life-engagement.html
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The medical school is situated near the most historic square mile in America. The campus is 13 square acres in the heart of Center City Philadelphia.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: The Office of Diversity and Inclusion Initiatives (ODII) at SKMC is dedicated to promoting an atmosphere in which diversity is celebrated and embraced. The ODII is a division of the Office of the Dean and works closely with all components of the medical school, providing support for diversity initiatives for faculty, students and staff of the Medical College.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: SKMC offers a range of resources to promote wellness among its student body. The Student Counseling Center provides services to support the emotional health and well-being of students through individual counseling and psychiatric services, wellness programming, outreach, and workshops.  The Office of Student Affairs, the Dean’s Advisory Council on Student Wellness (comprised of faculty, staff, and student representatives), and several student-run organizations offer programming and activities to support medical student well-being.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: In curricular, co-curricular and extracurricular activities, the culture at Sidney Kimmel Medical College is extremely collaborative. The Office of Student Life and Engagement provides opportunities for student engagement and personal growth. In collaboration with other offices within the Student Affairs Division, OSLE strives to address the holistic needs of students and create an environment of challenge and support, fostering student development.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: A car is required for Phase 2 and Phase 3 of the curriculum

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Medical students are expected to wear white coats whenever they are in patient areas.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Office of Student Affairs and Career Counseling works with students in need of academic support to match their needs with the resources available.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Patient interaction begins in the first week of classes in the first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: JeffMD is predominantly taught in small groups with active learning but does include some large group lectures.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: In the JeffMD curriculum, clinical rotations begin in April of the second year.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: No - but attendance is required for small group activities and patient panels.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The JeffMD curriculum was implemented in July 2017. The mission of JeffMD is to educate physicians who will serve, lead and discover. Phase 1 focuses on fundamental knowledge and skills and runs through April of the second year of the curriculum.  In this phase students have a longitudinal clinical experience, as well as a scholarly inquiry (continuing through Phase 2 and 3) and a humanities experience. The JeffMD curriculum has a reduced number of lectures and more small-group sessions focusing on problem-solving, evidence-based medicine, and service-based learning.  Phase 2 includes required core clinical clerkships and a research month.  Phase 3 focuses on the student's chosen specialty.  As a student, you will contribute to Sidney Kimmel Medical College’s proud tradition of excellence. You will have many opportunities to develop as a leader in your profession – in clinical settings, research labs and community service. You will find strong integration of clinical experience and science instruction throughout your four years here. In keeping with modern medical practice, you will gain the analytical skills to evaluate changing data and treatment options, sharpened emotional intelligence and comfort working in multi-specialty teams. The curriculum enables each student to achieve competence in biomedical and social sciences, clinical and research skills, and in the professional values, attitudes, and behaviors requisite for residency training and beyond. The tradition of providing a clinically balanced medical education includes an emphasis on students supporting and cooperating with each other.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: JeffMD provides excellent primary care exposure. In addition to the Physician Shortage Area Program co-curriculum which has dedicated fifty years to training students who plan to practice in rural areas, there is a co-curriculum called Jeff BEACON (Bringing Equity and Care for Our Neighborhoods). The Jeff BEACON Program promotes health equity for disadvantaged urban communities in Philadelphia. This program will train students to serve the needs of local communities, involve communities in research, and incorporate the expertise of community leaders in improving health. This program will provide training on delivering non-biased, culturally appropriate, trauma-informed care and seek to increase the diversity of health care professionals to better reflect the communities they serve. This co-curricular program is led by faculty members experienced in community-based primary care. Interested students may apply in the fall of their first year at SKMC.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Many clinical and basic science research opportunities are available for students, especially for the summer between first and second years, as well as for those students in the Clinical and Translational Research track.  At this time, more than 60% of graduates report that they have done some research during their four years in medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Community service is not required but is strongly encouraged.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Students are required to complete one or more projects over their four years of medical school. They choose a concentration of special interest from seven different Scholarly Inquiry tracks.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Our university hospital and its affiliated hospitals allow students to complete their core rotations in a number of settings, including urban, suburban and rural.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
In the preclinical curriculum, grades are Pass/Fail.
In the clinical curriculum grades are Honors, High Pass, Pass, Fail.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: As one of the oldest institutions of higher education in the nation, Thomas Jefferson University has, since its founding as the Jefferson Medical College in 1824, emphasized the attainment of clinical excellence in its educational programs. The name of Jefferson Medical College was changed to Sidney Kimmel Medical College on July 17, 2014.  A recent significant expansion of the research programs has created a balanced institutional mission and has enhanced the clinical instruction at Thomas Jefferson University Hospital and its affiliated hospitals.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Sidney Kimmel Medical College at Thomas Jefferson University is committed to: educating physicians who will form and lead the integrated healthcare delivery and research teams of tomorrow; discovering new knowledge that will define the future of clinical care through investigation from the laboratory to the bedside, and into the community; and setting the standard for quality, compassionate and efficient patient care for our community and for the nation. We recognize that a diverse community is imperative to achieving excellence in patient care, education, and research. As we carry out our mission, we are committed to the highest standards of professionalism and aspire to be a community of discovery, learning, and inclusion.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: The Penn State-Jefferson Premedical-Medical Program (PMM), founded in 1963, is a seven-year combined degree program with three years of undergraduate study at Penn State main Campus and four years at Sidney Kimmel Medical College. The Penn State B.S. degree is awarded after the first year of medical school and the Sidney Kimmel Medical degree is after year four of medical school. Applicants must have a minimum of 1470 SAT score or 32 ACT score to be considered.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: SKMC prefers to receive a recommendation from a preprofessional committee. If there is no such committee, letters should be provided by individual faculty members (preferably one letter each from Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Humanities, if possible). Applicants who have been involved in graduate programs are encouraged to provide additional letters from their graduate schools.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: One-on-one interview with a faculty member (open file) and one-on-one interview with a student (closed file). Interviews are held in-person.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: The EDP program should be a consideration by those applicants who strongly desire to attend SKMC and have an excellent academic record.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: Must have earned a baccalaureate degree from a US or Canadian university
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: Must have earned a baccalaureate degree from a US or Canadian university
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
1. All applications for admission to SKMC shall be received and processed by the
Admissions Office in preparation for action by the Committee on Admissions. A mission-aligned, 
holistic review of all qualified applicants will be undertaken by the Committee on Admissions.
2. The Committee on Admissions shall be responsible for the selection of all
students and shall have the authority to act in all matters pertaining to
admissions in accordance with general policies adopted by the faculty of the
college.
3. No applicant shall be admitted to SKMC without a personal interview by a
member of the Committee on Admissions.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Coursework completed at a community college is accepted.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Updates sent to SKMC.Admissions@jefferson.edu are accepted through 12/31/2026.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Applicants to Sidney Kimmel Medical College (SKMC) are selected based on academic credentials, extracurricular accomplishments, and personal characteristics critical for developing competent physicians. Additionally, certain minimum physical and cognitive abilities, defined here as technical standards, are deemed necessary to assure that candidates for admission, promotion, and graduation are able to complete the entire course of study, participate fully in all aspects of medical training, and ensure patient safety.  As requirements for admission, promotion, and graduation, a candidate for the MD degree at SKMC must possess the abilities and skills to meet these ten technical standards, with or without accommodations. Please click on the link to view those items on pages 119-120 of the SKMC Student Handbook.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Financial aid awards are based on need determined by a confidential analysis of information provided by the student and the student's family to the designated needs analysis service. If need is established, the student is directed to obtain a federally subsidized Stafford loan. If need exists beyond this loan program, Jefferson will try to meet a portion of this need from loan and grant funds. Applications for financial aid are available after December from the Office of Student Financial Aid. Completed financial aid applications for the next academic year must be submitted before April 1 or within two weeks of the date of acceptance.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition is prorated if a student has to discontinue their studies in a given year.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Recognizing that each college/university has a somewhat unique curriculum, we have changed our chemistry requirements from required to recommended to accommodate that variation.  We prefer two years of chemistry but how that is divided between general chemistry, organic chemistry and biochemistry is no longer defined.  Physics and biology requirements have also been changed to recommended courses.  Above and beyond the applicants' academic profile, SKMC looks favorably on applicants who have demonstrated strong interpersonal and intrapersonal competencies.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Jefferson, in accordance with local, state, and federal law, is committed to providing equal educational and employment opportunities for all persons, without regard to race, color, national and ethnic origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, disability, or veteran status. Jefferson complies with all relevant ordinances and state and federal statutes in the administration of its educational and employment policies. The selection of students is made after careful consideration of many factors, including the academic record, letters of recommendation, MCAT scores, and interview results regarding the applicant's personal qualities, motivation, interpersonal skills, and achievement in nonacademic areas. Sidney Kimmel Medical College is firmly committed to the educational goal of enrolling a diverse body of talented students.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Exposure to the medical field may be achieved through shadowing or through hands-on experiences such as medical assistant, patient care technician, certified nurse assistant, emergency medical technician, or other roles that enable interacting with patients, clients or community members.
